Predicates:
DeadlyDisease(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is a bile duct cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(x) ::: x is Cholangiocarcinoma.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is colorectal cancer.
FormOfCancer(x, y) ::: x is a form of y.
CameWithLowSurvival(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
IsBileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is bile duct cancer.
IsSevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
IsColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is colorectal cancer.

Premises:
∀x (DeadlyDisease(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: If something is a deadly disease, then it comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(cancer1) ∧ DeadlyDisease(cancer1) ::: Severe cancers are deadly diseases.
BileDuctCancer(bileDuctCancer1) ∧ FormOfCancer(bileDuctCancer1, cancer) ::: Bile duct cancer is a form of cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(cholangiocarcinoma1) ∧ FormOfCancer(cholangiocarcinoma1, bileDuctCancer) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma is bile duct cancer.
MildFlu(mildFlu1) ::: Mild flu comes with a low survival rate.
ColorectalCancer(colorectalCancer1) ∧ ¬(FormOfCancer(colorectalCancer1, bileDuctCancer) ∧ CameWithLowSurvival(colorectalCancer1)) ::: Colorectal cancer is not both a bile duct cancer and with a low survival rate.

Conclusion:
IsSevereCancer(colorectalCancer1)
